outcome: Cord blood gas parameters (pH, bicarbonate, base excess, pCO2, lactate)
Neonatal outcomes (maximum bilirubin concentration, need for phototherapy, need for clinical monitoring or admission to NICU)
cohort: 97 newborns delivered vaginally and 124 newborns delivered by cesarean section at term without fetal distress
finding: Three-minute delayed cord clamping leads to a shift towards mixed acidosis in cesarean deliveries and prevalent metabolic acidosis in vaginal deliveries, with a more pronounced increase in arterial lactate observed in cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: The study found that 3-minute delayed cord clamping resulted in a shift towards mixed acidosis in cesarean deliveries and prevalent metabolic acidosis in vaginal deliveries.
